en: lose after leading; blow a lead and lose

examples.ko: 우리 팀이 후반에 역전패해서 너무 속상해요.
examples.en: I'm so upset because our team lost after being ahead in the second half.
We narrowly lost a game we had been winning yesterday.
It's really disappointing to lose after leading 2-0.

examples.ko: 우리 반이 결승전에서 역전패할 줄은 몰랐어요.
examples.en: I never thought our class would lose the final after leading.

examples.ko: 역전패한 날에는 아무 말도 하기 싫어요.
examples.en: On the day we blow a lead and lose, I don't want to talk to anyone.

examples.ko: 역전패하지 않으려고 선수들이 끝까지 열심히 뛰었어요.
examples.en: The players ran hard until the end so they would not lose after leading.

explain: 그냥 '지다'와 달리 앞서 있다가 뒤집혀서 질 때만 써요. 반대말은 '역전승하다'이고, 주로 스포츠 뉴스나 경기 이야기에서 나와요.
explain_en: Unlike plain '지다' (to lose), this is only used when you were ahead and then lost. The opposite is '역전승하다', and it mostly appears in sports news and talk about games.

examples.ko: 어제 커피를 연거푸 세 잔이나 마셨어요.
examples.en: Yesterday I drank three cups of coffee in a row.
That player won the championship repeatedly in a row.
I made mistakes one after another and felt so embarrassed.
Maybe because I breathed in smoke, I coughed again and again.

examples.ko: 시험에서 연거푸 떨어져도 포기하지 않을 거예요.
examples.en: Even if I fail the exam repeatedly, I won't give up.

examples.ko: 연거푸 비가 와서 빨래를 못 말렸어요.
examples.en: It rained day after day, so I couldn't dry my laundry.

explain: '계속'은 오래 이어지는 느낌이고, '연거푸'는 같은 일이 짧은 간격으로 잇달아 여러 번 일어날 때 써요. 잔, 번, 실수처럼 셀 수 있는 일과 잘 어울리고, '연달아', '잇따라'와 비슷해요.
explain_en: '계속' (continuously) suggests something going on for a long time, while '연거푸' means the same thing happens several times in quick succession. It pairs well with countable things like cups, times and mistakes, and is close to '연달아' and '잇따라'.

examples.ko: 저는 이 대학 연구실에서 일하는 연구생이에요.
examples.en: I'm a research student working in a lab at this university.

examples.ko: 우리 연구실에는 연구생이 다섯 명 있어요.
examples.en: There are five research students in our lab.
To join as a research student, you need the professor's permission.

examples.ko: 그 형은 연구생 시절에 논문을 세 편 썼어요.
examples.en: He wrote three papers back when he was a research student.
The research students are doing experiments until late at night.
I'm still a research student, so there is a lot I don't know yet.

explain: 주로 대학 연구실에서 연구에 참여하는 학생을 말하지만, 바둑 연구생처럼 프로를 준비하는 사람에게도 써요. 분야에 따라 뜻이 조금 달라서 앞뒤 이야기로 알아야 해요.
explain_en: It mainly means a student taking part in research in a university lab, but it is also used for people preparing to turn pro, as in 바둑 연구생 (Go trainee). The meaning shifts a little by field, so check the context.

examples.en: I sliced the lotus root thin and made it into a braised side dish.
Boiled lotus root is crunchy when you chew it, so it's tasty.
I bought a bundle of lotus root at the market.

examples.ko: 연근 조림은 도시락 반찬으로 인기가 많아요.
examples.en: Braised lotus root is a popular side dish for lunch boxes.

examples.ko: 연근을 자르면 실 같은 것이 길게 늘어나요.
examples.en: When you cut lotus root, thread-like strands stretch out.

examples.ko: 연근 껍질은 칼로 벗기고 식초물에 담가 두세요.
examples.en: Peel the lotus root with a knife and soak it in vinegar water.

explain: 연꽃의 뿌리 부분을 먹는 채소로, 자르면 구멍이 여러 개 보여요. 간장에 졸인 '연근조림'이 반찬으로 가장 흔하고 튀김이나 전으로도 먹어요.
explain_en: It is the edible root part of the lotus, and you can see several holes when you cut it. The most common dish is soy-braised '연근조림' as a side dish, and it is also eaten fried or as jeon.

examples.en: That actor is very famous as a strong actor.
It's a movie with highly skilled actors, so I'm looking forward to it.

examples.ko: 아이돌 출신이지만 이제는 연기파라는 말을 들어요.
examples.en: She started as an idol, but now people call her a real actress.

examples.ko: 이 드라마에는 연기파 선배들이 많이 나와요.
examples.en: Many highly skilled senior actors appear in this drama.

examples.ko: 그분은 연기파답게 우는 장면을 정말 잘 소화했어요.
examples.en: True to being a strong actor, he handled the crying scene really well.

examples.ko: 연기파가 아니라고 걱정했는데 연기를 아주 잘하더라고요.
examples.en: I worried he wasn't a strong actor, but he acted really well.

explain: 외모나 인기보다 연기 실력으로 인정받는 배우를 말해요. '실력파'처럼 '-파'가 붙어 어떤 방식으로 인정받는 사람을 나타내고, 주로 '연기파 배우'로 써요.
explain_en: It refers to an actor recognized for acting skill rather than looks or popularity. Like '실력파', the '-파' ending marks a type of person, and it is mostly used as '연기파 배우'.

en: being born a year apart; two siblings a year apart in age

examples.ko: 저는 오빠와 연년생이고 학년도 하나 차이예요.
examples.en: My brother and I were born a year apart, and we're one grade apart too.

examples.ko: 연년생 아이 둘을 키우려니 정말 바빠요.
examples.en: Raising two kids born a year apart keeps me really busy.
We were born a year apart, so we get along like friends.

examples.ko: 연년생 동생이 있어서 옷을 같이 입어요.
examples.en: I have a sibling just a year younger, so we share clothes.
Brothers born a year apart fight a lot, too.
My older sister and I were born in consecutive years.

explain: 태어난 해가 한 해 차이인 형제·자매를 말해서, 생일에 따라 실제로는 몇 달밖에 안 차이 날 수도 있어요. 보통 '연년생 형제', '연년생 자매'처럼 쓰고, 쌍둥이와는 달라요.
explain_en: It describes siblings born in consecutive calendar years, so depending on birthdays they might be only a few months apart. It is usually used as '연년생 형제' or '연년생 자매', and it is different from twins.

examples.en: When spring comes, the mountains take on a light yellow-green color.
The fields in early spring are completely light green.
Light green sprouts have come up out of the ground.
The willow leaves sparkle yellow-green in the sunlight.
Wearing a light green dress makes it feel like spring.
Light yellow-green is a color that rests the eyes.

explain: 초록보다 밝고 노란 기운이 도는 봄 새잎의 색이에요. '연두색'과 거의 같게 쓰는데, '-빛'은 색이 비치는 느낌을 더해서 자연이나 풍경을 말할 때 잘 어울려요.
explain_en: It is the bright, slightly yellowish green of new spring leaves. It is used almost like '연두색', but '-빛' adds a sense of color glowing or showing through, so it suits nature and scenery.

examples.en: Gas prices went up, so fuel costs a lot.
With an electric car, you hardly worry about fuel costs.
In winter, the burden of heating fuel costs is big.

examples.ko: 한 달 연료비를 계산해 보니 십만 원이에요.
examples.en: I calculated a month of fuel costs and it's 100,000 won.
The company covers fuel costs for business trips.

examples.ko: 연료비는 차가 클수록 더 많이 나와요.
examples.en: The bigger the car, the higher the fuel cost.

explain: '기름값'은 일상에서 주유할 때 편하게 하는 말이고, '연료비'는 차뿐 아니라 난방·운송 같은 비용 전체를 말할 때도 써요. '연료비가 들다', '연료비를 아끼다'처럼 말해요.
explain_en: '기름값' is the casual word for the price of gas when you fill up, while '연료비' can also cover costs for heating or transport in general. Typical phrases are '연료비가 들다' and '연료비를 아끼다'.

examples.en: I sat by the pond and watched the fish.
The children play catching frogs at the edge of the pond.
In the evening I walked slowly along the pond.
We ate our lunch under the willow tree by the pond.
It rained, so the area around the pond is muddy.

examples.ko: 연못가 벤치는 우리가 자주 만나는 곳이에요.
examples.en: The bench by the pond is where we often meet.

explain: '강가', '바닷가', '길가'처럼 '-가'가 붙어 물 둘레의 가장자리를 말해요. '연못가에서', '연못가를 따라'처럼 장소를 나타내는 조사와 함께 자주 써요.
explain_en: Like '강가', '바닷가' and '길가', the '-가' ending means the edge or surroundings of the water. It often appears with place particles, as in '연못가에서' and '연못가를 따라'.

examples.en: The cherry blossoms have bloomed fully in light pink.
The sky is light pink because of the sunset.
The baby's cheeks are light pink, so they're really cute.
The bride in a light pink hanbok was beautiful.
Maybe because it's cold, the tip of your nose looks light pink.
A light pink lipstick suits spring well.

explain: 분홍보다 옅고 부드러운 색이에요. '연분홍색'이나 '연분홍'이라고도 하고, 꽃이나 볼, 하늘처럼 색이 은은하게 비치는 것을 말할 때 '-빛'을 잘 써요.
explain_en: It is a paler, softer shade than plain pink. People also say '연분홍색' or just '연분홍', and '-빛' is nice for things where the color glows gently, such as flowers, cheeks and the sky.

examples.ko: 이 기계는 연속적으로 열 시간을 돌릴 수 있어요.
examples.en: This machine can run continuously for ten hours.

examples.ko: 소리가 연속적이지 않고 중간중간 끊겨서 들려요.
examples.en: The sound isn't continuous; it comes in broken pieces.
Even after a series of failures, he didn't give up.

examples.ko: 이 만화는 연속적 그림으로 움직임을 보여 줘요.
examples.en: This comic shows movement through a continuous sequence of pictures.

examples.ko: 연속적 변화가 아니라 갑자기 바뀌는 거예요.
examples.en: It's not a gradual, continuous change; it switches suddenly.

examples.ko: 연속적으로 일어난 사고라서 원인을 찾기 어려워요.
examples.en: The accidents happened one after another, so the cause is hard to find.

explain: '연속적으로', '연속적인'처럼 이어지는 성질을 설명할 때 써요. 반대말은 '단속적'(끊겼다 이어졌다 하는)이고, '이틀 연속'처럼 횟수를 셀 때는 '연속'만 써요.
explain_en: It describes the quality of going on without a break, as in '연속적으로' and '연속적인'. The opposite is '단속적' (on and off), and when counting like 'two days in a row' you use just '연속'.

examples.ko: 올해 우리 회사에 연수생 열 명이 들어왔어요.
examples.en: Ten trainees joined our company this year.

examples.ko: 저는 해외 연수생으로 일 년 동안 일본에 있었어요.
examples.en: I was in Japan for a year as an overseas trainee.
The trainees receive training every morning.
I'm still a trainee, so there's a lot I don't know yet.
I explained the company rules to the trainee.

examples.ko: 한국어 연수생을 위한 수업이 따로 있어요.
examples.en: There are separate classes for Korean-language trainees.

explain: 회사나 기관에서 일을 배우거나, 어학연수처럼 일정 기간 교육을 받는 사람이에요. '연수'가 교육을 받는 일을 뜻해서 '연수를 받다'와 함께 자주 나와요.
explain_en: It means someone who learns the work at a company or institution, or takes a training program for a set period such as language study abroad. Since '연수' means training, it often appears with '연수를 받다'.

examples.ko: 눈 때문에 기차가 한 시간이나 연착했어요.
examples.en: The train arrived an hour late because of the snow.
The plane was delayed, so I was late for my appointment.
The bus often runs late, so leave early.

examples.ko: 안개가 심해서 배가 연착할 것 같아요.
examples.en: The fog is thick, so the ship will probably arrive late.

examples.ko: 열차가 연착하면 환불을 받을 수 있어요.
examples.en: If the train arrives late, you can get a refund.

examples.ko: 열차가 연착한다는 방송이 나오자 대합실이 술렁였어요.
examples.en: When the announcement came that the train was late, the waiting room buzzed.

explain: 기차, 비행기, 배, 버스가 정해진 시간보다 늦게 도착할 때 써요. 출발이 늦어지는 건 '연발'이라고 해서 서로 달라요. 일상에서는 그냥 '늦게 도착하다', '늦다'라고도 많이 말해요.
explain_en: Use it when a train, plane, ship or bus arrives later than scheduled. A late departure is called '연발', so the two differ. In daily talk people also just say '늦게 도착하다' or '늦다'.

examples.ko: 연초록을 좋아해서 가방도 그 색으로 샀어요.
examples.en: I like light green, so I bought my bag in that color too.
The light green leaves sparkle in the sunlight.
Wearing a light green T-shirt makes you look fresh.
The newly grown leaves are light green.
I painted the wall light green and the room became brighter.

examples.ko: 연초록과 노랑을 섞으면 더 밝은 색이 돼요.
examples.en: If you mix light green and yellow, you get a brighter color.

explain: 연두나 '연둣빛'과 가까운 밝은 초록이에요. 반대로 짙고 어두운 초록은 '진초록'이라고 해요.
explain_en: It is a bright green close to '연두' and '연둣빛'. A deep, dark green is called '진초록' by contrast.

examples.ko: 연필심을 너무 세게 누르면 자꾸 부러져요.
examples.en: If you press the pencil lead too hard, it keeps breaking.
Pencil lead is made from a material called graphite.

examples.ko: 연필심 끝이 뭉툭해서 글씨가 굵게 써져요.
examples.en: The tip of the lead is blunt, so my writing comes out thick.

examples.ko: 연필심이 다 닳으면 칼로 깎거나 새 연필을 쓰세요.
examples.en: When the lead wears down, sharpen it with a knife or use a new pencil.
Pencil lead dust got on my hand and made it black.
I wrote small letters with a sharp pencil lead.

explain: 연필 가운데의 까만 부분이에요. 샤프에 넣는 건 보통 '샤프심'이라고 불러서 구분해요. 그냥 '심'이라고만 해도 앞뒤 이야기로 알아들어요.
explain_en: It is the dark core in the middle of a pencil. The refill for a mechanical pencil is usually called '샤프심', which keeps the two apart. People may also just say '심' when the context is clear.

examples.en: I sent a New Year's card to my teacher again this year.
A pretty New Year's card arrived from a friend.
I carefully wrote New Year's greetings in the card.
These days people send greetings by text instead of New Year's cards.
It's good to mail New Year's cards at the end of December.
I made a New Year's card with a family photo on it.

explain: 새해 인사를 적어 보내는 카드예요. '새해 복 많이 받으세요' 같은 인사를 많이 쓰고, 요즘은 종이 카드 대신 메시지나 사진으로 인사하는 일이 많아요.
explain_en: It is a card you send with New Year's greetings. People often write something like '새해 복 많이 받으세요', and these days many send messages or images instead of paper cards.

examples.en: The fans cheered wildly at the concert hall.

examples.ko: 열광적인 응원 덕분에 우리 팀이 이겼어요.
examples.en: Thanks to the enthusiastic cheering, our team won.
The concert hall was full of a frenzied atmosphere.
The response isn't wildly enthusiastic, but it's quite good.

examples.ko: 신제품이 나오자 사람들이 열광적으로 줄을 섰어요.
examples.en: When the new product came out, people lined up with great excitement.
I came off the stage to rapturous applause.

explain: '열광하다'에서 나온 말로 환호, 응원, 박수, 반응처럼 사람들의 뜨거운 반응을 말할 때 써요. 비슷한 '열렬하다'는 사랑이나 지지의 마음을, '열광적'은 흥분이 겉으로 드러나는 모습을 더 말해요.
explain_en: Coming from '열광하다' (to go wild with excitement), it describes passionate reactions such as cheers, support, applause and responses. Similar '열렬하다' stresses the feeling of love or support, while '열광적' stresses visible excitement.

examples.en: I keep tropical fish in a tank at home.
Tropical fish live well in warm water.
Tropical fish have bright colors, so they're nice to watch.
Tropical fish swim among the coral.
I bought fish food at the tropical fish shop.

examples.ko: 열대어에게 하루에 두 번 먹이를 줘요.
examples.en: I feed the tropical fish twice a day.

explain: 따뜻한 지방에 사는 물고기로, 색이 화려해서 집이나 가게 어항에서 기르는 경우가 많아요. 물 온도에 민감해서 키울 때는 히터가 필요한 경우가 많아요.
explain_en: These are fish from warm regions, and since they are colorful, many are kept in tanks at home or in shops. They are sensitive to water temperature, so keeping them often calls for a heater.

examples.en: Mom made kimchi with young radish.
Young radish has soft leaves and stems.
I bought two bunches of young radish at the market.
Lightly salt the young radish and let it sit.
Eating young radish noodles in summer is refreshing.
The young radish was tender, so I put it raw in bibimbap.

explain: 일반 무와 달리 뿌리가 작고 가늘며, 잎과 줄기를 함께 먹는 어린 무예요. 여름에 열무김치로 많이 담가 먹어요.
explain_en: Unlike ordinary radish, it has small, thin roots, and you eat the leaves and stems along with it. It is often made into yeolmu kimchi in summer.

examples.en: In summer I eat noodles in yeolmu kimchi broth.
My mother made the yeolmu kimchi herself.
The yeolmu kimchi has fermented nicely and tastes tangy.
Yeolmu kimchi goes well with barley rice.

examples.ko: 열무김치 국물이 시원해서 자꾸 마시게 돼요.
examples.en: The yeolmu kimchi broth is so refreshing that I keep drinking it.

examples.ko: 열무김치 한 통을 이웃에게 나눠 줬어요.
examples.en: I shared a container of yeolmu kimchi with my neighbor.

explain: 어린 무인 열무로 담근 김치로 국물이 많은 편이고 여름에 즐겨 먹어요. 국수를 말거나 비빔밥에 넣어서 먹는 일이 많아요.
explain_en: This is kimchi made from young radish, and it usually has a lot of broth and is a summer favorite. People often put it in noodles or in bibimbap.

examples.ko: 한여름에 오래 밖에 있으면 열사병에 걸릴 수 있어요.
examples.en: If you stay outside for long in midsummer, you can get heatstroke.

examples.ko: 열사병을 예방하려면 물을 자주 마셔야 해요.
examples.en: To prevent heatstroke, you should drink water often.
A student collapsed from heatstroke on the field.

examples.ko: 열사병은 위험하니까 빨리 병원에 가야 해요.
examples.en: Heatstroke is dangerous, so you must go to the hospital quickly.
If heatstroke symptoms appear, move to the shade.
If you suspect heatstroke, call 119 right away.

explain: 더운 곳에서 체온이 너무 올라 생기는 위험한 병이에요. 가볍게는 '더위를 먹다'라고 말하는데, 어지럽고 기운이 없는 정도를 가리켜요.
explain_en: It is a dangerous condition where body temperature rises too high in hot conditions. For milder cases people say '더위를 먹다', meaning feeling dizzy and drained from the heat.

examples.en: The teacher taught the students with great dedication.

examples.ko: 모두 열성껏 준비한 덕분에 행사가 잘 끝났어요.
examples.en: Because everyone prepared with such dedication, the event went well.
Thank you so much for helping so wholeheartedly.
Many parents raise their children with great dedication.
We cheered with all our hearts, but sadly lost.

examples.ko: 새로 온 직원이 열성껏 일해서 칭찬을 받았어요.
examples.en: The new employee worked with enthusiasm and got praised.

explain: '열심히'는 어떤 일에든 쓰지만, '열성껏'은 마음과 정성을 다한다는 느낌이 더 강해요. 가르치기, 돕기, 응원하기처럼 남을 위한 일과 잘 어울려요.
explain_en: '열심히' fits almost any task, while '열성껏' carries a stronger sense of putting heart and effort into it. It suits things done for others, such as teaching, helping and cheering.

examples.en: I dyed my hair at home with hair dye.

examples.ko: 염색약 냄새가 너무 독해서 창문을 열었어요.
examples.en: The dye smell was so strong that I opened the window.

examples.ko: 염색약이 옷에 묻으면 잘 안 지워져요.
examples.en: If dye gets on your clothes, it doesn't come off easily.
I have a lot of gray hair, so I bought hair dye.
Be careful not to let the dye touch your skin.
I agonized over the dye color and chose brown.

explain: 주로 머리카락을 염색할 때 쓰는 약을 말해요. 옷감이나 천을 물들이는 재료는 보통 '염료'라고 해서 구분해요.
explain_en: It mainly means the product used to color hair. The material for coloring fabric or cloth is usually called '염료', which keeps the two apart.

examples.en: I secretly eavesdropped on the people next to me.

examples.ko: 남의 전화를 엿듣는 건 예의가 아니에요.
examples.en: It's rude to eavesdrop on other people's phone calls.
Don't eavesdrop at the door; come in.
My younger sibling was listening in on our talk.
The conversation I overheard at the cafe was so funny.

examples.ko: 누가 엿들을까 봐 작은 목소리로 말했어요.
examples.en: I spoke quietly in case someone was listening in.

explain: 남이 모르게 몰래 듣는다는 느낌이라, 우연히 들린 것은 '듣게 되다'로 말하는 편이 자연스러워요. '듣다'처럼 ㄷ 불규칙이라서 '엿들어요', '엿들었어요', '엿들은'으로 바뀌어요.
explain_en: It carries the feeling of listening secretly, so for something you just happened to hear, '듣게 되다' sounds more natural. Like '듣다' it is a ㄷ-irregular verb, giving '엿들어요', '엿들었어요' and '엿들은'.

en: be revealed; show through; be glimpsed

examples.en: You can sense his anxiety from the way he speaks.

examples.ko: 이 그림에는 작가의 따뜻한 마음이 엿보였어요.
examples.en: The artist's warm heart showed through in this painting.
You can catch a glimpse of the room through the gap in the door.
It was a face where sadness showed behind the smile.

examples.ko: 글 곳곳에서 그 사람의 성격이 엿보여서 재미있어요.
examples.en: His personality shows here and there in his writing, which is fun.
He was a child whose talent was visible from early on.

explain: 겉으로 다 드러나지 않고 일부만 슬쩍 보일 때 써요. 마음, 성격, 재능처럼 속에 있는 것에 많이 쓰고, 그냥 눈에 보이는 것은 '보이다'라고 해요.
explain_en: Use it when something is not fully out in the open but a part of it shows slightly. It is often used for inner things like feelings, personality and talent, while things simply visible to the eye are just '보이다'.

examples.en: I'm worried this injury might be permanent.

examples.ko: 영구적인 해결책은 아니지만 일단 이렇게 해 봐요.
examples.en: It's not a permanent solution, but let's try this for now.
That rule is permanent, so it doesn't change.

examples.ko: 영구적 보존이 필요한 문서는 따로 보관해요.
examples.en: Documents that need permanent preservation are stored separately.

examples.ko: 임시 거처라서 영구적으로 살 곳은 아니에요.
examples.en: It's temporary housing, so it's not a place to live permanently.

examples.ko: 이 일은 영구적이지 않아서 다른 일도 알아보고 있어요.
examples.en: This job isn't permanent, so I'm looking into other work too.

explain: 반대말은 '일시적'이나 '임시적'이에요. '영구적으로', '영구적인'처럼 쓰고, 일상 대화에서는 '영원히'나 '계속'이라고도 많이 말해요.
explain_en: Its opposites are '일시적' and '임시적'. It is used as '영구적으로' or '영구적인', and in daily talk people often say '영원히' or '계속' instead.

examples.ko: 몸이 약해서 영양식을 챙겨 먹고 있어요.
examples.en: My body is weak, so I make sure to eat nourishing food.
I cooked porridge as nourishing food for my grandmother.
When you're sick, you need nourishing food.
Samgyetang is the classic nourishing food for summer.

examples.ko: 시험 기간에는 영양식을 먹고 힘을 냈어요.
examples.en: During exam season I ate nourishing food to keep my strength up.
I made a nutritious lunch box and brought it along.

explain: 몸에 좋은 영양을 채우려고 먹는 음식이에요. '보양식'과 비슷한데, 보양식은 더위에 지친 몸을 보충하는 음식으로 삼계탕 같은 것을 말하는 일이 많아요.
explain_en: It is food eaten to take in good nutrition for the body. It is close to '보양식', which is often used for restorative dishes like samgyetang that help a body worn out by the heat.

examples.en: That director is very famous in the film world.
The film industry is going through hard times these days.
I'm studying acting to get into the film world.
People from the film world gathered at the awards ceremony.
Young directors in the film world are getting attention.
He left the film world and became a novelist.

explain: '-계'는 어떤 분야의 사람들과 세계를 묶어 부르는 말이에요. '연예계', '정치계', '학계'처럼 쓰고, '영화계'는 감독, 배우, 제작사까지 영화와 관련된 사람들 전체를 말해요.
explain_en: '-계' groups the people and world of a field together, as in '연예계', '정치계' and '학계'. '영화계' covers everyone connected to film, including directors, actors and producers.

examples.en: My friend is a well-known movie buff.
I'm a movie buff, so I go to the theater every weekend.
I went to a meetup where movie buffs gather.

examples.ko: 저는 영화광이 아니라서 유명한 배우도 잘 몰라요.
examples.en: I'm not a movie buff, so I don't know the famous actors well.

examples.ko: 영화광 삼촌이 추천해 준 영화를 봤어요.
examples.en: I watched the movie my movie-buff uncle recommended.

examples.ko: 영화광인 언니는 한 해에 백 편을 봐요.
examples.en: My older sister, a movie buff, watches a hundred films a year.

explain: 영화를 아주 좋아해서 많이 보는 사람이에요. '야구광', '축구광'처럼 '-광'이 붙으면 그것을 열렬히 좋아하는 사람이라는 뜻이 돼요.
explain_en: It is a person who loves movies and watches a lot of them. With '-광', as in '야구광' and '축구광', a word means someone who is passionately fond of that thing.

examples.ko: 송금할 때 예금주 이름을 꼭 확인하세요.
examples.en: Be sure to check the account holder's name when you transfer money.
Who exactly is the holder of this account?

examples.ko: 예금주 본인만 통장을 해지할 수 있어요.
examples.en: Only the account holder can close the account.

examples.ko: 예금주 이름이 달라서 이체가 안 됐어요.
examples.en: The transfer failed because the account holder's name was different.

examples.ko: 예금주님, 계좌 번호를 다시 알려 주세요.
examples.en: Account holder, please tell me the account number again.
The holder of this account is my mother.

explain: 통장이나 계좌의 주인을 말해요. 송금할 때 '예금주 확인'이 나오고, 일상에서는 '계좌 주인'이라고도 말해요.
explain_en: It means the owner of a bank account or passbook. '예금주 확인' (account holder check) appears when you transfer money, and in daily talk people may also say '계좌 주인'.

examples.en: There are about six or seven students in the classroom.

examples.ko: 예닐곱 살쯤 된 아이가 울고 있었어요.
examples.en: A child around six or seven years old was crying.
I bought about six or seven apples at the market.
You only need to go about six or seven stops from here.

examples.ko: 초대한 친구가 예닐곱은 올 것 같아요.
examples.en: I think about six or seven of the friends I invited will come.

examples.ko: 예닐곱 번 해 보면 익숙해질 거예요.
examples.en: If you try it six or seven times, you'll get used to it.

explain: 정확한 수를 모를 때 여섯이나 일곱쯤이라고 어림해서 말해요. '대여섯'(다섯이나 여섯)처럼 비슷한 말이 있고, 보통 '예닐곱 명', '예닐곱 개'처럼 단위와 함께 써요.
explain_en: You use it to estimate roughly six or seven when you don't know the exact number. There is a similar word, '대여섯' (five or six), and it is usually used with a counter, as in '예닐곱 명' or '예닐곱 개'.

examples.ko: 그 가수의 본명은 예명과 완전히 달라요.
examples.en: That singer's real name is completely different from the stage name.
I use a stage name when I sing.
The stage name is far more famous than the real name.
The singer performs under a stage name, so I don't know the real name.
I was curious what the stage name meant, so I looked up an interview.
Can I call you by your real name instead of your stage name?

explain: 가수나 배우가 활동할 때 쓰는 이름이에요. 짝이 되는 말은 '본명'이고, 글 쓰는 사람이 쓰는 이름은 '필명'이라고 해서 구분해요.
explain_en: It is the name a singer or actor uses while performing. Its counterpart is '본명' (real name), and the name a writer uses is called '필명' (pen name).
